Lauren Pinkston

Independent candidate for Governor, Tennessee · Open seat

Counter-human trafficking researcher and practitioner; former university business professor and elementary school teacher

Lauren Pinkston is a 39-year-old independent candidate for Governor of Tennessee who lives in Columbia, in Maury County. She was formerly an assistant professor at Lipscomb University and has worked in anti-trafficking research and nonprofit work. This is her first run for public office, and she is listed as an Independent Candidate for governor on the November 3, 2026 general election ballot.

Where Pinkston stands

Education
Opposes the universal school voucher (Education Freedom Scholarship) expansion. Would keep the state's older voucher programs and move the expansion money to early childhood education and child care, saying the state is 90,000 child care slots short.
Abortion / Reproductive health
Says she "believes all life is sacred" but has criticized Tennessee's total abortion ban for criminalizing physicians. Says health care decisions should lie with the patient and the doctor, with social supports to save lives.
Health care
Proposes expanding postpartum Medicaid coverage on the Wisconsin model, expanding primary care through telehealth, nurse practitioners and PAs, taking on pharmacy benefit managers, and legalizing medical cannabis.
Economic development / Data centers
Proposes a "data dividend" funded by high-producing data companies in Tennessee. Supports a moratorium on new data centers until siting rules are in place.
Debates
Agreed to debate independent David Hatley on October 27 at Middle Tennessee State University.

Background

  • Candidate for Governor of Tennessee (Independent), 2026: her first campaign for public office
  • Assistant Professor of Business as Mission, Lipscomb University (2019–2023)
  • Founded businesses employing trafficking survivors in Southeast Asia (2015–2019)
  • Doctoral research internship, UN Office on Drugs and Crime, Laos (2015)
  • Former elementary school teacher
  • PhD, International Family and Community Studies, Clemson University (2019)
  • B.A., Freed-Hardeman University (2009)
  • Endorsed by the Forward Party (April 2026)
